title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from pages 92-94. E (and E') is a set with a symmetric 'orthogonality' relation x |o| y. This relation gives a Galois-type closure operator supp°_E on subsets of E: closed sets are the 'supports', and each support is the orthogonal of its orthogonal. Σ_E is the complete lattice of supports. In it, Sup^{Σ_E}(S_i) = supp°_E(∪ S_i), and σ_E(x) = supp°_E({x}). A 'correspondence' α : E → P(E') induces ᾱ(A) = ∪_{x∈A} α(x) and α_*(S) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(S)) on supports. Prop. 4 of § C lists equivalent conditions (i)-(iv) on α. Condition (iv) is the existence of a 'transpose' β : E' → P(E) with x |o| β(x') ⇔ α(x) |o| x'. Condition (v) says that α_* : Σ_E → Σ_{E'} commutes with arbitrary Sups (v a), plus α_*(σ_E(x)) = supp°_{E'}(α(x)) (v b).

This page does two things.
(1) It finishes the proof that (i)-(iv) imply (v). For a family S_i in Σ_E, (ii) lets one remove the inner closure: α_*(supp°(∪ S_i)) = supp°_{E'}(∪ ᾱ(S_i)) = supp°_{E'}(∪ supp°_{E'} ᾱ(S_i)) = Sup_i α_*(S_i).
(2) For the converse, it checks the 'variant' α_*(supp°_E(A)) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(A)) for arbitrary A ⊂ E. Write supp°_E(A) = Sup_{x∈A} σ_E(x) and apply (v a). On the other side, supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(A)) = Sup_{x∈A} supp°_{E'}(α(x)). The two agree provided α_*(σ_E(x)) = supp°_{E'}(α(x)). Grothendieck notes this is exactly v b), a clause he had to add after the fact.

Then comes a 'Scholie' (first headed 'Cor.'). Corr(Σ, Σ') is the set of maps Σ → Σ' commuting with arbitrary Sups (hence monotone). The next page states the canonical bijections Corr(Σ_E, Σ_{E'}) ≅ Corr(E, E') ≅ Corr*(E, E'):
- Corr(E, E') consists of maps α : E → Σ_{E'} satisfying Prop. 4.
- Corr*(E, E') consists of relations R ⊂ E×E' with every R(x) ∈ Σ_{E'} and every tR(x') ∈ Σ_E.
- The maps are φ(α_*) = α_* ∘ σ_E, and ψ(α) = {(x, x') : α(x) |o| x'}, the graph composed with orthocomplementation.

In modern terms: sup-lattice morphisms between the closure (concept) lattices of two polarities correspond bijectively to relations whose rows and columns are all closed sets. These are the 'bonds' of formal concept analysis, equivalently morphisms in the category of sup-lattices / Chu-type spaces. The purpose seems to be building a category of 'orthogonality spaces' (possibly as models for 'ateliers'), with morphisms described concretely.
errors: No substantive error. The step α_*(supp°(∪S_i)) = supp°(ᾱ(∪S_i)) relies on condition (ii) (images of supports are compatible with closure), which is used implicitly.

Notational drift: on p. 92 the closure is written int°_E, here supp°_E. The draft also shows the author discovering that v b) must be added as a separate clause to (v) for the converse; this is a correction he made himself, not an error.

ideas.what: Lattice Σ_E of closed sets ('supports') of a set with a symmetric orthogonality relation; Sup = closure of the union
ideas.modern_name: Closure lattice of a polarity / orthogonality space (Galois closure), concept lattice
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); Foulis-Randall and Dacey (orthogonality spaces); Wille (concept lattices, 1982)

ideas.what: Correspondences α with transpose β defined by x |o| β(x') ⇔ α(x) |o| x'
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint / transposable relation (Galois connection between orthogonality spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Galois connection theory (Ore, Birkhoff); Chu-space duality

ideas.what: Bijection between sup-preserving maps Σ_E → Σ_{E'} and relations R ⊂ E×E' whose rows and transposed columns are closed
ideas.modern_name: Bonds between formal contexts ↔ sup-morphisms of concept lattices; morphisms in Sup / Chu
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shmuely (1974, Galois connections and tensor products of complete lattices); Ganter-Wille, Formal Concept Analysis (1996/99, 'bonds')

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently reformulates the bond/sup-lattice-morphism correspondence for symmetric orthogonality spaces, including the subtlety that the relation is the graph of α composed with orthocomplementation. The result itself is known (Shmuely 1974; Ganter-Wille bonds), so this is only a historical curiosity.
missed.quote: Ainsi ψ(α) n'est pas le graphe de la correspondance donnée α ..., mais de la correspondance déduite en composant avec c_{Σ'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck working on concept-lattice / Chu-type structures in his late period. It does not add new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a correct but known lattice-theoretic correspondence (polarities, bonds, sup-lattice morphisms). The only interest is the historical fact that Grothendieck rediscovered it in his 1986 notes.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the image reads '= supp°_{E'} ∪_i supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(S_i)) = Sup_i α_*(S_i), ok'; the brace labels the inner term α_*(S_i). This is consistent with the transcription, but differs from the int° notation of the previous page.
'Il reste : prouver que (v) implique la variante.' The next line looks like '[?] sur le fermeture C(i) §' and remains largely illegible.
'c'est v b), que j'ai dû just ajouter après coup' is more plausibly 'c'est v b), que j'ai dû y rajouter après coup'.
In the displayed formula for supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(A)), a struck-through 'supp' precedes 'supp°_{E'} α(x)'.
The heading reads 'Cor.' with 'Scholie,' written above a struck-out 'Soit'.
The parenthetical reads '(appelées les "correspondances" de Σ : Σ')' and the next line '(Elles sont donc croissantes), et'.
